back: One named, timed operation (an HTTP handler, a DB query) with trace ID, span ID, parent ID, start and end time, kind, attributes, events and status.
All spans sharing one trace ID, linked into a tree by parent span IDs: the full path of one request.

front: Why does one service call make two spans?
back: A CLIENT span in the caller and a SERVER span in the callee. The difference is time outside the callee's code: network, pools, proxies, retries.

front: Why can spans hold an order ID when metric labels can't?
back: Each span is one stored record, not a new time series, so high-cardinality attributes don't multiply storage.
version-traceid-parentid-flags, e.g. 00-<32 hex trace ID>-<16 hex parent span ID>-01. The low flag bit means sampled.
tracestate carries vendor-specific trace data next to traceparent. baggage (a separate W3C header) carries app key-values to every downstream service.
OpenTelemetry code that injects the current context into outgoing headers and extracts it from incoming ones.

front: Where does trace propagation usually break?
back: Message queues, thread pools and async callbacks, proxies that strip unknown headers, and services using a different header format such as B3.
The root decides whether to record the trace and propagates the sampled flag. Cheap and consistent, but keeps errors only at the sample rate.
Record every span, buffer, decide when the trace is complete: keep errors and slow traces. Costs buffer memory and routing by trace ID.
QPS × spans per trace × bytes per span × 86,400. 20,000 × 25 × 300 B ≈ 13 TB/day unsampled.
The common OTel head sampler: roots sample 1% by trace ID; every other span follows its parent's decision, so traces are never half-recorded.
API, SDK, instrumentation libraries, OTLP (gRPC 4317, HTTP 4318), the Collector, and semantic conventions.
Vendor neutrality: instrument once and change back ends via Collector config. Costs: another component to run, tuning, overhead.
The chain of spans that determined end-to-end latency. Speeding up spans off it, such as parallel work that finished early, gains nothing.

front: CLIENT span 1,950 ms, SERVER span 1,100 ms. Where did 850 ms go?
back: Outside the callee: connection-pool wait, TLS handshake, retries, proxy or load-balancer queueing, or network.

front: A child span starts before its parent. Why?
back: Clock skew between hosts. Trust durations within one span over gaps between spans on different machines.
